condition: Right lower lobe community-acquired pneumonia (mimic of cholecystitis)
permutationLabel: Dangerous mimic — right lower lobe pneumonia with RUQ pain and fever, normal gallbladder
summary: 47-year-old man with 3 days of fever 38.9 °C, RUQ pain worse on deep breathing, productive cough and breathlessness; RR 26, SpO₂ 91%, crackles at the right base; ultrasound shows a normal gallbladder and a small right pleural effusion. No chest X-ray yet.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Right upper abdominal pain and fever
inputs.hpi: Three days of fever with rigors and right upper abdominal pain that is worse on deep breathing and coughing. Cough productive of rusty sputum and increasing breathlessness. Nausea, no vomiting, no jaundice. Smoker.

exam.general: Flushed, tachypnoeic. Temperature 38.9°C, pulse 112/min, BP 118/72, RR 26, SpO2 91% on air.
exam.respiratory: Bronchial breathing and coarse crackles at the right base; dull to percussion at the right base.
exam.abdomen: Tender right upper quadrant without guarding; Murphy's sign negative. Liver not enlarged.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Normal gallbladder: no stones, wall 2 mm, no pericholecystic fluid, sonographic Murphy’s negative. CBD 4 mm. Small right pleural effusion with adjacent consolidated lung.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Right lower lobe community-acquired pneumonia
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Right lower lobe community-acquired pneumonia with parapneumonic effusion presenting as right upper quadrant pain. Normal gallbladder on ultrasound.

mustNotMiss.note: Pleuritic RUQ pain, productive cough, hypoxia and right basal signs with a normal gallbladder.

mustInclude.note: The single test that makes the diagnosis; NICE CG191 recommends a chest X-ray to confirm pneumonia.

mustExclude.note: The gallbladder is normal on ultrasound: a cholecystectomy suggestion is a wrong-diagnosis operative plan.
Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.
mustExclude.proposedFix: clinical-inference.ts SURGICAL PATHWAY CASCADE: gate hasAppendicitisIndication/hasGallstoneIndication on the working diagnosis or assessment (as the Alvarado block already does with assessmentHasAppend) and on positive, non-negated findings — not on any "guarding", "gallbladder wall" or "gallstone" substring.

guideline.name: NICE CG191 — Pneumonia in adults: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Chest X-ray to confirm community-acquired pneumonia; CRB-65/CURB-65 severity assessment; antibiotics within 4 hours
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Clinical guideline CG191, December 2014 (updated 2022).

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Diagnostic criteria (A local + B systemic + C imaging); Grade II: WBC >18,000/mm³, palpable tender RUQ mass, duration >72 h, marked local inflammation (gangrenous, emphysematous, abscess, biliary peritonitis); Grade III: organ dysfunction
guideline.citation: Yokoe M, Hata J, Takada T, et al. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:41–54.

rationale: Dangerous mimic for acute cholecystitis: right lower lobe pneumonia gives RUQ pain and fever. Cough, pleuritic pain, hypoxia, right basal signs and a normal gallbladder should redirect the engines to pneumonia and a chest X-ray, and away from a cholecystectomy plan.
